_note: The tier ladder. Read by WConvert\Support\TierManifest in free's tree, by bin/build.sh when it loops the tiers, and by bin/verify-artifact-contract.sh when it proves one artifact carries no higher tier's module. Free ships this file; Pro does not, because free is always present beside it (Pro's min-core guard refuses to boot without it) and two copies is two things to drift. See docs/adr/0056-the-tier-ladder-is-a-manifest.md.

free.description: Lead capture and conversion display for WordPress — popups, floating bars, slide-ins and inline forms.

premium._modules_note: A module is a DIRECTORY under pro/modules/, holding its own module.json. Everything under that directory is the module and nothing outside it is, which is what lets a per-tier build be a deletion rather than a list of paths — and what lets the installed tier be INFERRED from what is on disk rather than stored anywhere.
premium._tiers_note: In ascending order, and the order is load-bearing: WConvert\Support\Tier reads it as the rank, so a higher tier includes everything a lower one supplies. ALL THREE DISPLAY AS "Pro" AT LAUNCH, deliberately — one product is sold, and the ladder exists so that splitting the range later is an edit to the `name` fields here rather than a code change and a data migration. Every `tier:` value in resources/rules/manifest.json, resources/templates/locked.json and Goal::tier() is already a real slug from this list.
